decision.explanation: Integration by parts with u=(ln x)^2 and dv=x^{-3}dx gives −(ln x)^2/(2x^2)+∫(ln x)/x^3 dx. Applying integration by parts again gives −(ln x)^2/(2x^2)−ln(x)/(2x^2)−1/(4x^2)+C, which is option d. Differentiating verifies the integrand.

after.worked_solution:
We need to use integration by parts.

In this case, we define

$$
\begin{aligned}u={ln}^{2}⁡(x)\, & ⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{2\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)}{x} \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{{x}^{3}}\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x=\int \frac{1}{{x}^{3}}\,\text{d}x=-\frac{1}{2{x}^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{{ln}^{2}⁡x}{{x}^{3}}\,\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =({ln}^{2}⁡(x))(-\frac{1}{2{x}^{2}})-\int (-\frac{1}{2{x}^{2}})(\frac{2\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)}{x})\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\frac{{ln}^{2}⁡(x)}{2{x}^{2}}+\int \frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)}{{x}^{3}}\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

We use integration by parts once again to evaluate $\int \frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)}{{x}^{3}}\text{d}x.$ We take

$$
\begin{aligned}u=\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)\, & ⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{x} \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{{x}^{3}}\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x=\int \frac{1}{{x}^{3}}\,\text{d}x=-\frac{1}{2{x}^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

In this case, the formula for integration by parts gives

$$

We need to use integration by parts.

In this case, we define

$$
\begin{aligned}u={ln}^{2}⁡(x)\, & ⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{2\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)}{x} \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{{x}^{3}}\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x=\int \frac{1}{{x}^{3}}\,\text{d}x=-\frac{1}{2{x}^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{{ln}^{2}⁡x}{{x}^{3}}\,\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =({ln}^{2}⁡(x))(-\frac{1}{2{x}^{2}})-\int (-\frac{1}{2{x}^{2}})(\frac{2\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)}{x})\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\frac{{ln}^{2}⁡(x)}{2{x}^{2}}+\int \frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)}{{x}^{3}}\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

We use integration by parts once again to evaluate $\int \frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)}{{x}^{3}}\text{d}x.$ We take

$$
\begin{aligned}u=\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)\, & ⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{x} \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{{x}^{3}}\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x=\int \frac{1}{{x}^{3}}\,\text{d}x=-\frac{1}{2{x}^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

In this case, the formula for integration by parts gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{{x}^{3}}\,\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =(\operatorname{ln}⁡(x))(-\frac{1}{2{x}^{2}})-\int (-\frac{1}{2{x}^{2}})(\frac{1}{x})\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)}{2{x}^{2}}+\frac{1}{2}\int \frac{1}{{x}^{3}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)}{2{x}^{2}}-\frac{1}{4{x}^{2}}+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C$ is an integral constant.

So we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{{ln}^{2}⁡x}{{x}^{3}}\,\text{d}x & =-\frac{{ln}^{2}⁡(x)}{2{x}^{2}}+(-\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)}{2{x}^{2}}-\frac{1}{4{x}^{2}}+C) \\  & =-\frac{{ln}^{2}⁡(x)}{2{x}^{2}}-\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)}{2{x}^{2}}-\frac{1}{4{x}^{2}}+C \\  & =-\frac{1}{4{x}^{2}}(2{ln}^{2}⁡(x)+2\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)+1)+C.\end{aligned}
$$

\begin{aligned}u=5{x}^{2}+1\, & ⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=10x \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=\operatorname{sin}⁡x\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x=\int \operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x=-\operatorname{cos}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 5{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =(5{x}^{2}+1)(-\operatorname{cos}⁡x)-\int (-\operatorname{cos}⁡x)(10x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =-(5{x}^{2}+1)\operatorname{cos}⁡x+10\int x\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}u=x\, & ⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=1 \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=\operatorname{cos}⁡x\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x=\int \operatorname{cos}⁡x\,\text{d}x=\operatorname{sin}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

In this case, the formula for integration by parts gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\int x\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =(x)(\operatorname{sin}⁡x)-\int (\operatorname{sin}⁡x)(1)\,\text{d}x \\  & =x\operatorname{sin}⁡x-\int \operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & =x\operatorname{sin}⁡x+\operatorname{cos}⁡x+D,\end{aligned}
$$

\begin{aligned}\int (5{x}^{2}+1)\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x & =-(5{x}^{2}+1)\operatorname{cos}⁡x+10(x\operatorname{sin}⁡x+\operatorname{cos}⁡x+D) \\  & =-(5{x}^{2}+1)\operatorname{cos}⁡x+10x\operatorname{sin}⁡x+10\operatorname{cos}⁡x+10D \\  & =(9-5{x}^{2})\operatorname{cos}⁡x+10x\operatorname{sin}⁡x+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C=10D.$

content.worked_solution:
We need to use integration by parts. 

In this case, we define

$$
\begin{aligned}u=5{x}^{2}+1\, & ⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=10x \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=\operatorname{sin}⁡x\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x=\int \operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x=-\operatorname{cos}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 5{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =(5{x}^{2}+1)(-\operatorname{cos}⁡x)-\int (-\operatorname{cos}⁡x)(10x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =-(5{x}^{2}+1)\operatorname{cos}⁡x+10\int x\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Again, we use integration by parts to evaluate  $\int x\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,\text{d}x.$ We take

$$
\begin{aligned}u=x\, & ⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=1 \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=\operatorname{cos}⁡x\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x=\int \operatorname{cos}⁡x\,\text{d}x=\operatorname{sin}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

In this case, the formula for integration by parts gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\int x\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =(x)(\operatorname{sin}⁡x)-\int (\operatorname{sin}⁡x)(1)\,\text{d}x \\  & =x\operatorname{sin}⁡x-\int \operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & =x\operatorname{sin}⁡x+\operatorname{cos}⁡x+D,\end{aligned}
$$

where $D$ is an integral constant.

So we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (5{x}^{2}+1)\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x & =-(5{x}^{2}+1)\operatorname{cos}⁡x+10(x\operatorname{sin}⁡x+\operatorname{cos}⁡x+D) \\  & =-(5{x}^{2}+1)\operatorname{cos}⁡x+10x\operatorname{sin}⁡x+10\operatorname{cos}⁡x+10D \\  & =(9-5{x}^{2})\operatorname{cos}⁡x+10x\operatorname{sin}⁡x+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C=10D.$
